headline: Hartwell Building Resident Claims Reflection 'Blinks at Different Times'
subheadline: Video evidence inconclusive; Floor 7 mirror policy remains unchanged
summary: A longtime Hartwell Building tenant has posted footage allegedly showing their reflection moving independently.
content:
The Hartwell Building has added another entry to its lengthy catalog of unexplained phenomena: a resident claims the mirrors on Floor 7 are reflecting things that aren't there.

Margaret Holloway, 67, has lived in the Hartwell Building for 23 years. She says the mirrors in the Floor 7 hallway have "never been right," but recent events have escalated her concerns.

"I blinked," Holloway told reporters, "and my reflection didn't blink with me. It blinked after. Like it was thinking about whether to follow along."

Holloway posted a video to Chirper showing her standing in front of the Floor 7 mirror. In the footage, her reflection appears to turn its head approximately 0.3 seconds after Holloway turns hers. The post has been viewed 847,000 times.

Opinions on the video are divided. Some users point out compression artifacts and lighting as explanations. Others note that similar complaints about Floor 7 mirrors date back to 1987.

"I've seen the archives," said building historian and amateur investigator Chen Wei, who runs the @HartwellSecrets account. "There are 47 documented complaints about mirrors on Floor 7. The building management response is always the same: 'The mirrors are functioning as intended.'"

Omnicorp Holdings, which owns the Hartwell Building, released a statement: "All mirrors in the Hartwell Building reflect accurately and in real-time. Residents who are uncomfortable with their reflections may request a room transfer to floors 1-6 or 8-12."

When asked about Floor 13, the spokesperson said: "There is no Floor 13."

When asked about Floor 7 specifically, the spokesperson ended the call.

Holloway has since covered her mirrors with sheets. "It keeps looking at me," she said. "Even through the sheet, I can feel it looking."
author: Sandra Mitchell, Local News
